assumptions: Every arrow of M is monic.
Every endomorphism of every object of M is its identity.
A subobject of D is an equivalence class of monomorphisms into D under isomorphism of domains; its order is factorization.
The relation on object isomorphism classes is the usual reachability relation: [A] <= [B] if an arrow A -> B exists.

events.outcome: The displayed map is well-defined and injective under (i) and (ii).
events.reasoning: By (i), each u:D' -> D represents a subobject. If u and v represent the same subobject, there is an isomorphism a:D' -> D' with u = v composed with a. This a is an endomorphism, so (ii) gives a = id_D' and hence u = v. The image consists exactly of subobjects whose representing domain is isomorphic to D': for a representative m:X -> D and an isomorphism b:D' -> X, the arrow m composed with b has the same subobject class. Only triviality of automorphisms is needed for the injectivity step; (ii) supplies it.

events.outcome: Reachability is a partial order on isomorphism classes under (ii).
events.reasoning: Existence of an arrow is unchanged when either endpoint is replaced by an isomorphic object, by composing with the endpoint isomorphisms. Identities give reflexivity and composition gives transitivity. For arrows f:A -> B and g:B -> A, (ii) gives g composed with f = id_A and f composed with g = id_B. Thus f is an isomorphism with inverse g, and [A] = [B]. This establishes antisymmetry. Hypothesis (i) is not needed for this argument.

events.outcome: Isomorphic representatives have a unique M-isomorphism, yielding a distinguished, coherent order isomorphism between their subobject posets.
events.reasoning: For isomorphisms a,b:A -> B, b^{-1} composed with a is an endomorphism of A, hence the identity by (ii), so a = b. Existence comes from the assumption that A and B represent the same isomorphism class. For the unique isomorphism a, define T_a([m:X -> A]) = [a composed with m:X -> B]. Isomorphisms preserve monicity under composition. Any domain isomorphism witnessing equality of representatives continues to witness equality after composition with a. A factorization m = n composed with h becomes a composed with m = (a composed with n) composed with h, so T_a preserves order. T_(a^{-1}) is its inverse, so it also reflects order. Finally T_id is the identity and T_(b composed with a) = T_b composed with T_a; these equations give coherent transport under changes of representative. This proves a canonical induced isomorphism, without classifying arbitrary abstract order isomorphisms.

events.outcome: The category with two parallel arrows satisfies both hypotheses and has a nontrivial automorphism of Sub(B). This refutes only uniqueness among all abstract poset isomorphisms, not necessarily the author's intended canonical meaning of 'à isom unique près'.
events.reasoning: Define M with objects A,B; Hom(A,A) = {id_A}, Hom(B,B) = {id_B}, Hom(A,B) = {f,g} with f distinct from g, and Hom(B,A) empty. Identity compositions define all possible composites and satisfy the category axioms. The identities are monic. To test either f or g for monicity, each set Hom(X,A) has at most one member, so any parallel arrows into A are equal before composition. The only endomorphisms are identities. All arrows into B are f, g, id_B. The first two define distinct subobjects because their only possible domain automorphism is id_A; neither is equivalent to id_B because A and B are not isomorphic. Both lie below [id_B]. If [f] <= [g], a factorization would require f = g composed with h for h:A -> A, forcing h = id_A and f = g, a contradiction; the reverse comparison is equally impossible. Thus Sub(B) has exactly two incomparable elements [f],[g] below one greatest element. Swapping [f] and [g] and fixing [id_B] is a nonidentity order automorphism. The canonical transport induced by id_B is instead the identity.
